Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/checkpoint

# Checkpoint — record session context

Persist the **reasoning layer** of this work session (goal, decisions, dead ends,
constraints, next step) to the Obsidian vault, keyed to the current worktree.
Files are plain markdown written directly — no MCP, no Obsidian required running.

## Steps

### 1. Resolve where to write
Run the helper from the current worktree:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

It prints `TICKET`, `BRANCH`, `WORKTREE`, `SESSION_DIR`, `CONTEXT_FILE`,
`LOG_FILE`, `STAMP`, `CONTEXT_EXISTS` and creates the folders. **Only write to the
`CONTEXT_FILE` and `LOG_FILE` paths it gives you** — never elsewhere in the vault.
If it errors (not a git repo / detached HEAD), tell the user and stop.

### 2. Read existing context if present
If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, read `CONTEXT_FILE` first so you UPDATE it rather than
overwrite history. Digest sections get rewritten; accreting sections get appended.

### 3. Gather the reasoning layer
Reconstruct from this session's conversation + git. If a ticket id is present and
Linear is available, you may fetch the title/URL with `mcp__linear-server__get_issue`.
Apply the **extraction rubric** below to decide what is worth recording.

### 4. Write `_context.md`
Use the template at `~/.claude/skills/checkpoint/template.md` as the structure.
- If new file: fill the template. Set `created`/`updated` to today, `sessions: 1`.
- If updating: rewrite digest sections (TL;DR, Approved plan, Current state, Next
  step, Open questions, key_files, status), **append** to accreting sections (Key
  decisions, Dead ends, Constraints, Gotchas, Interventions) with a dated bullet,
  bump `updated` to today and increment `sessions`.
- **Approved plan:** write it only when the user approves a plan (gate 1), verbatim
  as approved: Mermaid diagram, per-file/module intent bullets, and the exact line
  `ship_when_verified: yes|no` (`no` unless the user said ship when verified).
  /create-pr parses this heading and line; don't rename or reformat them.
- **Interventions:** append `- [YYYY-MM-DD] <what the human had to do> — <why the agent couldn't>`
  whenever the user had to step in.

### 5. Append a log snapshot
Write a short dated entry to `LOG_FILE` (a fresh file — no append needed):
a 3–6 line summary of what THIS session accomplished + what changed since last time.
This is the immutable audit trail; `_context.md` is the living digest.

### 6. Confirm
Tell the user what you wrote (context file + log file paths) and the one-line Next step.

## Extraction rubric — what to record (keep it concise)

**The test:** record a line only if it would otherwise have to be *re-derived* or
would prevent *repeating a mistake*. Ask: *"What do I know now that I didn't at
session start, that isn't already in Linear, git, or the code?"*

**DO record (the reasoning layer — it evaporates when the session ends):**
- Scope agreement: how the ticket was interpreted, what's in/out of scope.
- Decisions: what + why + what was rejected + what would make us revisit it.
- Dead ends: what was tried that failed, and why.
- Constraints/preferences the user stated ("ship by Fri", "don't touch billing").
- Gotchas: environmental facts learned the hard way.
- Next step + open questions + current status.

**Do NOT record (noise / lives elsewhere):**
- Activity logs ("edited foo.ts, ran tests") — record outcomes, not keystrokes.
- Anything copy-pasteable from the diff, git history, or the Linear ticket body.
- Resolved questions — delete them or fold the answer into a decision.
- Restating how the code works — that's what the code is for.

**Mark uncertainty** explicitly (`*assumed*`, `*unchecked*`). Prefer 8 sharp lines
over 40 vague ones — this must stay skimmable for the user, not just parseable by an agent.

Don't add single-use wrapper functions. - Before review, run `dg-pr-adherence-check` and `scope-check`. ## Gotchas / landmines - Anything rendered outside `dropdownRef` triggers the capture-phase `window` outside-click dismissal, which deletes the pending arrow. - The Settings tab keeps its own `useState` copy of the settings, so a triple added from the canvas appears there only after the tab remounts. That's acceptable. - Another worktree's dev watcher can overwrite the vault plugin build. Grep the bundle before trusting a CDP run. ## Current state Not started, and blocked until the ENG-2256 branch exists. ## Next step Reset onto the ENG-2256 branch. --- ticket: ENG-2258 ticket_url: https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2258/create-a-discourse-relation-from-canvas-and-associate-it-with-the title: Create a discourse relation from canvas and associate it with the selected node type pair branch: eng-2258-create-a-discourse-relation-from-canvas-and-associate-it worktree: .claude/worktrees/eng-2258-create-a-discourse-relation-from-canvas-and-associate-it status: in-progress created: 2026-09-27 updated: 2026-09-27 sessions: 1 key_files: - apps/obsidian/src/components/RelationshipTypeSettings.tsx # private ColorPicker (~22-99) and validation (~116-161) to extract - apps/obsidian/src/components/ModifyNodeModal.tsx # pattern for a Modal with a React root (~634-693) - apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx # wire "Create new"; stop window listeners dismissing the menu while the dialog is open - apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/relationTypeUtils.ts # the ENG-2257 pair-link helper to reuse tags: [ai-session] --- > **TL;DR** This is the third and final PR of the stack (2256 → 2257 → **2258**), **based on the ENG-2257 branch**. `Create new` opens an "Add relation type" dialog with label, complement and colour. Continue creates the type, links it to the pair through the ENG-2257 helper, refreshes the menu and shows two toasts. ENG-2259 was merged into this ticket. This PR also carries the end-to-end verification for the parent ticket, ENG-2255. ## Goal / scope agreement - The overall plan and shared decisions are in `AI_sessions/eng-2255-implement-canvas-relation-creation-for-unconfigured-node/_context.md`. Read it first. - Design: DES-349 Case 2 mockup. The dialog is titled "Add relation type" with placeholders "Label (e.g., supports)" and "Complement (e.g., is supported by)", a colour dropdown defaulting to Black, and Cancel / Continue buttons. - **Out of scope:** full relation management in Settings, and linking types to other node-type pairs. ## Approved plan ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Create new"] --> B[CreateRelationTypeModal
label / complement / color] --> C[validate: required + no duplicate label/complement] C --> D[push DiscourseRelationType generateUid 'rel'] --> E[ENG-2257 associate helper] --> F[saveSettings once] --> G[refresh menu + 2 toasts] ``` - Extract `ColorPicker` from `RelationshipTypeSettings.tsx` into a shared component, for example `components/ColorPicker.tsx`. Settings imports it and behaves exactly as before. - Extract the label/complement validation into a pure function (required fields, duplicate label, duplicate complement). Settings behaviour stays the same. Don't tighten the matching (trim or case) unless you flag it as a separate decision. - New dialog: an Obsidian `Modal` with a `createRoot` React root, following `ModifyNodeModal`. Pass it `plugin`, the pair and an `onCreated` callback. Show errors with the existing `input-error` / `text-error text-xs` classes. - On Continue: 1. Build `{ id: generateUid("rel"), label, complement, color, created, modified }` with no `status`. 2. Associate the type with the pair through the ENG-2257 helper, saving only once if possible. 3. Close the dialog, refresh the dropdown list, and show both toasts: "Relation type created", then "Discourse relation added" with description `{label} relation added for {source type} and {target type}`. - Dropdown and overlay: while the dialog is open, the dropdown's capture-phase `window` `pointerdown` and Escape listeners must do nothing. Otherwise a click or Escape in the modal dismisses the menu and **deletes the pending arrow**. Use a ref flag checked in both listeners, or skip events whose target is inside `.modal-container`. When the dialog is cancelled, the arrow and menu stay open. ship_when_verified: no ## Key decisions - **[2026-09-27] ENG-2259 was merged into this ticket.** *Why:* DES-349 Case 2 is one flow, and creating a type without associating it is a dead end. Linear is updated: new title and Done When, and ENG-2259 is a Duplicate. - **[2026-09-27] Use an in-canvas dialog, not a redirect to Settings.** This is John's call on DES-349; later changes will follow user feedback. - **[2026-09-27] Cancelling the dialog keeps the arrow and the menu.** - **[2026-09-27] After Continue, the menu returns to the list view.** Don't apply the new type automatically; this matches the Case 2 mockup, step 3. ## Constraints & preferences - **Base branch:** straight after `/start`, before any commits, run `git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/eng-2257-add-an-existing-discourse-relation-from-relation-menu`, or use the local branch. Open the PR against the ENG-2257 branch. `/create-pr` reads its target branch from the main checkout, so check it before pushing. - The target size is 400 lines or fewer, excluding tests. If it goes over, the Reviewer brief must explain why the PR can't be split. - Code comments are one or two lines at most. Don't add single-use wrapper functions. - Before review, run `dg-pr-adherence-check` and `scope-check`. ## Gotchas / landmines - Escape inside an Obsidian Modal can't be stopped from the DOM, because the modal uses a keymap scope. The dropdown's `window` capture listener runs **before** the modal handles Escape, so the guard has to be in the dropdown. - The Obsidian 1.13 `.setting-item` card and the Tailwind preflight gaps apply if Settings markup is used inside the modal. - Another worktree's dev watcher can overwrite the vault plugin build. Grep the bundle before trusting a CDP run. - In CDP, tldraw ignores programmatic `store.put` for autosave, so drive real pointer and keyboard input. ## Current state Not started, and blocked until the ENG-2257 branch exists. ## Next step Reset onto the ENG-2257 branch. Extract `ColorPicker` and the validation, with Settings behaviour unchanged, and then build the modal. ## Verification - Run throwaway scratchpad unit tests for the extracted validation (empty fields, duplicate label or complement) and for building the type plus triple. Don't commit them. - Run `pnpm -C apps/obsidian ci:validate` or the repo equivalent. - Run `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` scenarios: 1. **Empty pair, Create new.** Fill in the dialog → Continue. Both toasts appear, the new type is in the menu without a reload, and picking it creates the relation with the correct colour and arrow text. 2. **Populated pair.** "+" → Create new works the same way. 3. **Validation.** A duplicate label or complement shows an error and saves nothing. 4. **Dialog doesn't dismiss the menu.** Clicking inside the dialog and pressing Escape to close it both leave the pending arrow and the menu in place. Cancel does the same. 5. **Settings regression.** Settings → Relation types: the colour picker and duplicate validation still work, and the new type is listed after the tab remounts. 6. **ENG-2255 end to end.** From a fresh vault with no triples for the pair, go from dragging an arrow → Add existing, and separately → Create new, through to a usable relation. Capture the screenshots for `pr-evidence`. ## Open questions / blockers - None.

  - `div.pointer-events-auto.absolute.z-30.-translate-x-1/2.-translate-y-1/2`: position absolute, z-index 30. It creates a stacking context (positioned with a z-index). Computed transform is `none`, because Tailwind translate utilities do nothing in Obsidian (no preflight). Its inline style is `left:615px; top:295px`.
  - `div.pointer-events-none.absolute.inset-0` (DragHandleOverlay root): absolute, z-index auto. No stacking context.
  - `span` (tldraw's in-front wrapper, no class): static, z-index auto. No stacking context. Its children, in order, are `.tl-canvas`, an unnamed absolute div, and the overlay.
  - `div.tl-container`: relative, z-index auto. No stacking context.
  
  **2. Chain from the style panel to `.tl-container`**
  - `div.tlui-style-panel.tlui-style-panel__wrapper`: relative, z-index 300 (its own stacking context).
  - `div.tlui-layout__top__right`: static, z-index auto.
  - `div.tlui-layout__top`: static, z-index auto.
  - `div.tlui-layout`: relative, z-index 300, with a transform matrix and `contain: strict`. This is the stacking context that matters for the panel.
  - `div.tl-container`: z-index auto.

  - Neither `.tl-container` nor `.tldraw__editor` creates a stacking context. The shared one is Obsidian's `.workspace-leaf` (`isolation: isolate; contain: strict`).
  - Inside it, the dropdown root competes at z-index 30 against `.tlui-layout` at 300 (tldraw's `--layer-panels`).
